Theory

Music theory practice: drills and printable exercise sets, a page for each chapter of Robert Hutchinson’s open textbook Music Theory for the 21st-Century Classroom, and real scores with expert Roman-numeral analyses.

Music theory practice, in three parts. Use the list on the left to move around, or Previous and Next at the foot of each page to go through it like a book.

Drills and exercises

  • Theory Drills: every drill on the site in one place: notes, intervals, key signatures, chords, Roman numerals and more. Each has its own settings, and a link can open a drill with your settings.
  • Exercise Builder: choose chapters and build a set of exercises, answered on the page or printed.

The textbook, chapter by chapter

Each page goes with a chapter of Robert Hutchinson’s open textbook Music Theory for the 21st-Century Classroom. Read the chapter there first, then practise here.

Chapter Page
1 Basic Concepts (from do to letter names)
2 Major Scales and Key Signatures (from movable do)
3 Minor Scales and Key Signatures (from la)
4 Basics of Rhythm (from du de)
5 Intervals (from syllable pairs)
6 Triads
7 Roman Numerals
8 Seventh Chords
9 Harmonic Progression
10 Non-Chord Tones
11 Melodic Analysis
12 Form in Popular Music
14 Accompanimental Textures
16 Figured Bass
17 Secondary Dominants
18 Secondary Diminished Chords
19 Mode Mixture
20 The Neapolitan Chord
21 Augmented Sixth Chords
22 Modulation
31 Jazz Theory

Analysed scores

Analysed Scores: real pieces with experts’ Roman numerals under the notes, one piece per page, to play along with: Bach’s “O Haupt voll Blut und Wunden” and the first movement of Beethoven’s “Moonlight” Sonata.
